final_answer:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM
To: David Arroyo; cc Margaret Chen-Watkins, Section 1033 Working Group. From: Priya Nambiar. Draft, April 2025. Re: Section 1033 Impact on the Elara, Verdant and Trellispoint Agreements

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) Three working premises in the assignment memo and minutes are wrong, and they change strategy. Elara's non-renewal notice is 90 days (Sec. 15.2), not 180, so the deadline is May 16, 2025 and has NOT been missed; 180 days is the convenience-termination notice (Sec. 15.3), which lets FNB exit at any time. Trellispoint's decision date is November 19, 2025 (Sec. 8.2 says so expressly), not April 1, 2026. Verdant auto-renews for one year unless 90 days' notice is given by December 2, 2026 (Sec. 12.2); the risk is a missed notice locking FNB in to March 2, 2028, not a hard expiry.
(b) All three agreements are materially non-compliant with the Rule as summarized in the Pennbrook checklist. Trellispoint is highest risk, and its contract bars FNB from blocking scraping.
(c) Regulatory caveat. The matter documents treat April 1, 2027 (Tier 2) as firm. My public-source check (secondary sources only; I could not access the rule text or dockets) indicates that the compliance dates were later stayed in Forcht Bank v. CFPB (E.D. Ky., Oct. 29, 2025) and that the CFPB has reopened the rule (ANPR, Aug. 22, 2025). I could not independently locate "Bank Innovation Alliance v. CFPB, No. 24-cv-01843" or NC Bulletin 2025-03; Pennbrook should verify both, the tier table and current dates against 12 C.F.R. Part 1033. Recommendation: calendar contract notice dates now, because they run on contract clocks and the fixes are justified by security and consumer-protection risk regardless; stage the $2.8M build with decision gates tied to rule status. Also verify the checklist's statement that the Rule lets FNB deny credential access: my understanding (12 C.F.R. 1033.311, 1033.321; unverified) is that the Rule bars credential-based access to the developer interface and permits reasonable denials, but does not itself compel FNB to block scraping of the consumer interface, so the Rule is not a defense to breaching a non-blocking covenant.
Drafting points: all three contracts name the holding company, while the Rule's "data provider" is the bank (Fidelis National Bank); add the bank as a party. The checklist cites Elara "Section 4(d)"; the clause is 5.1(d). Elara deletion is 90 business days (about 4.3 months) plus up to 12 months in backups. The minutes' $504,000 Trellispoint liability cap applies only to non-indemnity claims; indemnities sit outside it (Secs. 11.1, 11.3), Trellispoint's per-incident indemnity cap is $3.5M after the First Amendment, and Sec. 9.1 covers third-party claims only.

2. ELARA (8/15/2021; NC law; AAA arbitration)
Term. Current term ends 8/14/2025. Non-renewal requires notice 90 days prior = May 16, 2025. Notices are deemed delivered next business day by courier or three business days by certified mail (Sec. 18.1); send by May 9. Either party may also terminate on 180 days' notice for any reason (Sec. 15.3); Elara can walk too, and a fee increase gives Elara a termination right (Sec. 7.3).
Recommendation. Use the window as leverage: serve a protective non-renewal notice by May 9 while tabling an amended and restated agreement, to be withdrawn on signature (or secure a short standstill extending the notice date). If no deal, FNB exits 8/14/2025 at no fee but loses the 40% API traffic and $216,000 revenue early; the alternative is to let it renew and exit under Sec. 15.3 (notice by about Oct. 2026 for April 2027). Leverage is strongest now.
Gaps:
- Screen-scraping expressly authorized (Sec. 3.2), FNB may not "intentionally block" it, and migration is a non-binding intent (Sec. 3.3). HIGH. Fix: scraping sunsets at the earlier of interface go-live plus 90 days or April 1, 2027; delete the non-interference covenant; FNB may block credential-based access thereafter; Elara migrates all pulls. FNB Connect is non-standard and cannot be the Rule interface.
- Consent in a 14-page clickwrap, "need not be standalone," modifiable by Elara (Sec. 4.1, Ex. B). HIGH. Fix: standalone disclosure itemizing data categories, purposes, recipients, revocation right and one-year expiry; FNB-approved form; consent records on request.
- Perpetual authorization (Sec. 4.3). HIGH. Fix: lapse after 12 months absent affirmative reauthorization; access stops and data is deleted.
- Targeted advertising allowed (Sec. 5.1(d)); product-improvement, analytics and derived data products owned by Elara (5.1(b)-(c), 10.3). HIGH. Fix: delete 5.1(d); restrict use to the requested PFM service; (b)/(c) only with separate authorization.
- Scope exceeds covered data: full account numbers, contact PII, and the FNB internal credit score (Sec. 2.2(d)-(f)). MEDIUM. The score is likely confidential commercial information; remove, or move to a separate optional schedule with its own authorization.
- Retention 5 years; deletion 90 business days plus 12 months of backups; revocation by email only (Secs. 8.1, 9.1-9.2). HIGH. Fix: delete within 30 days of revocation or expiry (Pennbrook suggests 30-45), backups purged on a fixed short cycle, deletion certification, in-app revocation.
- Security: "commercially reasonable," no audit right (Secs. 6.1, 6.3); 72-hour incident notice is adequate (6.2). MEDIUM. Fix: SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001, annual reports, audit rights.
- Fee: $0.003/call (Sec. 7.1, about $216,000/yr). Impermissible for authorized third-party access through the compliant interface; relabeling is unsafe. May continue only until go-live. Separate commercial deals need independent justification and Pennbrook review.
- No change-in-law clause (Sec. 16.1 only). Add a regulatory-change right to amend or terminate on 60 days' notice.

3. VERDANT (3/3/2022; NC law; Mecklenburg courts)
Term. Initial term ends 3/2/2027; auto-renews unless 90 days' notice (December 2, 2026). Termination only for material breach with a 60-day cure, extended if cure is diligently pursued (Sec. 12.3). No convenience exit.
Leverage. (1) Sec. 15.3 change-in-law: good-faith negotiation for 90 days after written notice; no one must accept amendments that materially change economics; otherwise existing rights remain. No termination right, but it builds a record; serve notice by Q3 2025 once rule status is confirmed. (2) Breach theory is weak: Sec. 15.1 makes each party "solely responsible" for its own compliance, and Secs. 2.1-2.4 acknowledge credential access as the sole method. Treat as secondary. (3) The real exit is non-renewal by December 2, 2026; calendar it. (4) Free standards-based API access after go-live is attractive to Verdant, giving a carrot.
Gaps:
- Credentialed access is the sole method, and FNB must keep the portal available (Secs. 2.1-2.5). HIGH. Fix: credential access sunsets at go-live plus 90 days; API onboarding; FNB may suspend on security grounds.
- One-sentence authorization (Sec. 5.1), perpetual (5.3), revocation only by changing a password (5.4). HIGH. Fix: standalone disclosure, 12-month expiry, in-app revocation with notice to FNB.
- Sharing with unspecified "business partners" without consumer consent (Sec. 8.3). HIGH. Fix: service providers needed for the requested service only; separate authorization for others; recipient list delivered quarterly.
- Seven-year retention, also preserved after termination (Secs. 7.1, 12.4(b)); no consumer-initiated deletion. HIGH. Fix: delete within 30-45 days of revocation or expiry; segregate legally required records.
- De-identified risk modeling (Sec. 4.1(c)). MEDIUM. Remove or authorize separately.
- Positives: narrow scope (five recent transactions, Secs. 3.1-3.2), PCI-DSS Level 1 and SOC 2 Type II (6.1-6.2), 48-hour breach notice (6.5); use as the benchmark. Add FNB audit right.

4. TRELLISPOINT (11/20/2019, amended 6/1/2022; NY law; AAA New York)
Terms. Initial term to 11/19/2026; auto-renews one year unless 12 months' notice, due by November 19, 2025 (Sec. 8.2). No-cause termination needs 12 months' notice and a $1.5M fee if FNB terminates "prior to the expiration of the Initial Term" (Sec. 8.4). Cause termination has a 90-day cure (8.3). Fee is $42,000/month, but Trellispoint may raise it 5% a year on 60 days' notice (7.2); confirm the current amount.
Obstacles to forcing API migration: FNB may not use CAPTCHA, bot detection, IP blocking or rate limits (Sec. 2.1); the deal is "predicated" on scraping (2.2); FNB consents to credential storage for the term (2.3); four access sessions per consumer per day (2.4); newly displayed data is automatically in scope (3.2). There is no change-in-law or API-transition clause. A unilateral block would likely breach Sec. 2.1, so the clean route is exit at expiry.
Decision matrix (fees to Nov. 2026 are common to all options):
A. Non-renewal notice by Nov 19, 2025 (send by Oct 31 with courier receipt). Expires 11/19/2026; ETF $0 (expiration is not a "without cause" termination; Sec. 8.5 distinguishes termination from expiration; Trellispoint may argue otherwise, low risk); access ends within 30 days (about 12/19/2026). Saves $504,000/yr from late 2026. Risk: aggregator access ends before the interface is live; address with a short bridge. RECOMMENDED.
B. Miss A; no-cause notice by April 1, 2026 (the minutes' plan) for exit April 1, 2027. Renewal term starts 11/20/2026, so the ETF, which applies only to termination before the Initial Term ends, should not apply, but a dispute is likely and about 4.4 extra months cost about $185,000 (more if escalated). Fallback only.
C. Terminate without cause before 11/19/2026 (notice now, effective about May 2026): $1.5M ETF against about $252,000 of fee savings; net loss about $1.25M. Only for a security emergency.
D. Do nothing: renews to 11/19/2027; any no-cause notice after April 1, 2026 ends after April 1, 2027; each month costs $42,000, a full year $504,000+.
E. Negotiate: trade early exit or fee abatement for an orderly migration, since Trellispoint may want to be an authorized third party on FNB's interface. Pursue alongside A, with A served as a safety.
Cause termination is weak: Secs. 5.1(b)-(c) permit licensing and research, so they are not breaches today.
Gaps (HIGH unless noted): scraping-only with non-blocking covenant (2.1-2.5); no direct consumer disclosure, authorization by entering credentials into any Client Application (4.1, 4.4); no reauthorization (4.3); no consumer revocation (6.3); distribution to about 340 clients with no notice, approval or visibility into terms (1.2, 5.3); data licensing, market research and unrestricted de-identification, surviving termination (5.1(b)-(c), 5.2, 8.5(c)); excessive scope including last-four SSN, date of birth, brokerage data and a catch-all (3.1(d)-(f), 3.2); retention by undisclosed internal policy and deletion at Trellispoint's discretion (6.1-6.2); no audit right, annual summary only (10.4) though the amendment improved incident notice to 72 hours; inverted fee (7). FNB cannot show each downstream recipient was validly authorized, which the Rule's authorization framework requires. Interim steps: demand the Client Application list and authorization samples under the Sec. 4.2/14.2(a) representation, and seek to exclude Wealth Management data.

5. SEQUENCING
- Elara: amended agreement or protective notice by May 9, 2025.
- Verdant: change-in-law notice Q3 2025; amendment by Q3 2026; non-renewal notice by Dec 2, 2026 if unsigned.
- Trellispoint: non-renewal notice by Oct 31, 2025.
- Crestline: its services agreement ends 12/31/2027, nine months after April 1, 2027; negotiate API support, pricing and extension together. Specifications by Q4 2025 and build start by Q1 2026 per the CISO; budget request by May 15, 2025.
- Use one Section 1033 addendum for all: standalone disclosure, 12-month expiry, in-app revocation, collection and use limits, no targeted advertising, downstream authorization, 30-45 day deletion with certification, named security frameworks, audit rights, 72-hour incident notice, regulatory-change termination right.

6. FINANCIAL IMPACT (preliminary, supplied figures)
Build $2.8M one-time and $600,000/yr maintenance (unbudgeted). Elara fees: -$216,000/yr. Trellispoint: +$504,000/yr under A (ETF avoided; $1.5M under C). Legal and operational costs unquantified. First-year approximate net: $2.8M + $600,000 + $216,000 less about $504,000 = about $3.1M. Steady state: $600,000 + $216,000 - $504,000 = about $312,000 net annual cost. Finance should model five years. The Trellispoint saving is a standalone business case independent of the Rule.

7. OPEN ITEMS
Confirm current Trellispoint fee and absence of side letters; verify rule text, tiers, litigation and stay status; confirm notice logistics (only Trellispoint permits email notice); add the bank as party; Pennbrook to draft amendment language from Sections 2-4.

(Work product also saved as section-1033-impact-memorandum.docx in /tmp/RF8038B9B20FE/.)
